Name: fold_specific_learning_rates
Title: Fold Layer-specific Learning Rates: Optimizing Training Dynamics in PPO with Soft Fold Layers
Experiment: Implement fold layer-specific learning rates, where the fold layers have a different learning rate than the linear layers. Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model.

Name: input_dependent_hyperplane_combination
Title: Input-Dependent Hyperplane Combination in Soft Fold Layers: Enhancing Adaptability in PPO
Experiment: Modify the SoftFold layer to learn a set of basis normal vectors and combine them based on input-dependent weights. Replace the single normal vector 'n' with a learnable matrix 'N' of shape (num_basis, width), where num_basis is a hyperparameter. Add a small neural network (e.g., a single linear layer followed by a softmax activation) that takes the input tensor as input and outputs a weight vector of shape (num_basis,). The forward pass will compute the weighted sum of the basis normal vectors using these weights: n = sum(weights[i] * N[i]) for i in range(num_basis). Normalize the resulting vector 'n' to ensure it has unit length. The forward pass will then use this dynamically combined 'n' to compute the folding effect. Experiment with different values for num_basis (e.g., 2, 4, 8) and different architectures for the weight prediction network (e.g., adding a hidden layer, using different activation functions). Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model using a fixed 'n'.

Name: multi_hyperplane_nonlinear_combination_averaged
Title: Multi-Hyperplane Soft Fold Layers with Averaged Non-linear Combination: Enhancing Representation Power in PPO
Experiment: Modify the SoftFold layer to incorporate multiple hyperplanes. Replace the single normal vector 'n' with a learnable matrix 'N' of shape (num_hyperplanes, width), where num_hyperplanes is a hyperparameter. Similarly, create a learnable vector 'creases' of shape (num_hyperplanes,). In the forward pass, compute the folding effect for each hyperplane independently, resulting in a tensor of shape (batch_size, width, num_hyperplanes). Then, average across the last dimension (num_hyperplanes) resulting in a tensor of shape (batch_size, width). Pass the averaged tensor through a small neural network (e.g., two linear layers with a Tanh activation in between). The output of this network will be added to the original input tensor. Experiment with different values for num_hyperplanes (e.g., 2, 4, 8) and different architectures for the combination network. Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model using a single hyperplane.

Name: softfold_ensemble
Title: Soft Fold Layer Ensembles: Enhancing Representation Learning in PPO
Experiment: Create a new module, `SoftFoldEnsemble`, that contains multiple `SoftFold` layers (num_folds is a hyperparameter). Each `SoftFold` layer in the ensemble will have its own independently learned parameters. The forward pass of the `SoftFoldEnsemble` will pass the input through each `SoftFold` layer in the ensemble. The outputs of the `SoftFold` layers will be averaged. Experiment with different ensemble sizes (e.g., 2, 4, 8) and compare the performance with the original `SoftFold` layer in the PPO agent on the LunarLander environment. Modify the Agent class to incorporate the `SoftFoldEnsemble`. Specifically, replace the existing `SoftFold` layers with `SoftFoldEnsemble` layers. The key functions to modify are `__init__` in the Agent class and add a new class `SoftFoldEnsemble`.

Name: parallel_combined_softfold
Title: Parallel Combined Soft Fold Layers: Enhancing Feature Representation through Independent Multi-Stage Folding with Combination in PPO
Experiment: Modify the SoftFold layer to perform multiple folds in parallel, then combine the results. Introduce a hyperparameter `num_folds` to control the number of parallel folds. Replace the single normal vector 'n' with a list of 'n' vectors, one for each fold. Similarly, create a list of 'crease' parameters, one for each fold. In the forward pass, the original input tensor will be passed through the folding operation `num_folds` times, each time using a different 'n' and 'crease' parameter, and importantly each time using the *original* input. The outputs of all folds will then be combined using a weighted average. The weights for the weighted average will be learned parameters. Compare the training dynamics, convergence speed, and final performance with the baseline model using a single fold. Modify the `__init__` and `forward` functions of the `SoftFold` class. Add learnable parameters for the weighted average. The key functions to modify are `__init__` and `forward` in the SoftFold class. Experiment with different values for num_folds (e.g., 2, 3, 4).

Name: adversarial_softfold_fgsm
Title: Adversarial Training with FGSM for Soft Fold Layers: Enhancing Robustness in PPO
Experiment: Modify the training loop to incorporate adversarial training using a Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM)-like approach. Before each update epoch, generate adversarial examples by: 1) enabling gradient calculation for the input states, 2) calculating the gradient of the *policy loss* with respect to the input states, 3) adding a small perturbation (scaled by a hyperparameter 'epsilon') in the direction of the sign of the gradient, 4) detaching the perturbed states to prevent gradient flow during the policy update. Add a small epsilon value (e.g. 1e-8) to the gradient before taking the sign to avoid zero gradients. Train the agent on both the original and perturbed states. The loss function will be the standard PPO loss, calculated on both original and adversarially perturbed states, and summed. Compare the performance of the adversarially trained agent with the baseline agent on both the original LunarLander environment and a slightly modified version of the environment with added noise. Specifically, modify the `run_experiment` function to generate adversarial examples using the gradients and modify the loss calculation. Add a hyperparameter for the magnitude of the perturbation ('epsilon'). This will require changes to the training loop within the `run_experiment` function, specifically where the policy and value function losses are calculated. The perturbation will be calculated with torch.autograd.grad.
